messages:
olivia: FYI customer (AcmeRetail) is seeing a short burst of 504s and 502s to the hosted inference endpoint over the last 20m, started after a heavy batch job. They pasted a trace and we're seeing connection resets from the edge.

samir: Can you drop the minimal repro and any correlation ids? Also did they mention SDK version / region?

olivia: Region: us-west-2, SDK: js v3.1.2. Correlation: req-id=cr-7f6b2a. They say it started ~11:06 PST and lasted ~6 minutes. Their stack is serverless workers behind a NAT gateway.

taylor: Quick question — is this only streaming endpoints or gen as well?

olivia: Both, but streaming suffers more (clients see partial chunks then 504). Non-streaming requests sometimes return 502 mid-response.

nate: Assigning to eng-infra oncall; possible NAT session eviction / ephemeral IP churn. I saw similar with short-lived ephemeral connections when workers scale up.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-1376, priority P2. Assigned: eng-infra.

samir: Can the customer capture an edge request/response dump? If they can't, ask them to curl our endpoint with --http2 and include --verbose. Suggest adding header `x-rw-debug: true` and send the req-id.

olivia: They ran this reproducer and attached logs:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "x-rw-debug: true" \
  --http2 \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Customer log excerpt:
```
[11:06:12] -> POST /v1/generate req-id=cr-7f6b2a
[11:06:12] <- 200 chunk1 req-id=cr-7f6b2a
[11:06:13] <- connection reset by peer
[11:06:13] -> retry
[11:06:14] <- 504 gateway timeout req-id=cr-7f6b2a
```

taylor: Edge logs matching req-id show an upstream reset from the pool and a TCP RST from the client side shortly after. Likely short-lived NAT mapping lose. I'm seeing similar in our internal telemetry as NAT churn in that AZ spiking at 11:05-11:12.

nate: For immediate mitigation: ask customer to set SDK to prefer HTTP/1.1 or configure keepalive: false for short-lived worker tasks. That prevents HTTP/2 multiplexed streams from suffering session eviction when the underlying NAT mapping flips.

julie: Noted. I'll send a customer note with repro steps + mitigation. Draft:

"Thanks — we're seeing a transient networking issue in us-west-2 that can cause streaming connections to drop when NAT mappings rotate during scaling events. Workarounds: 1) prefer HTTP/1.1 for short-lived jobs, 2) disable persistent keepalives in the SDK, or 3) add a short retry with jitter on 5xx/504 for idempotent reads. Our infra team is investigating and we'll update you in 30m."

olivia: Customer tried forced http1 and saw stable results for the next 15m. They reverted to normal and spike returned. Customer ok with workaround for now — asking for ETA.

samir: Eng-infra findings so far: a specific NAT gateway in the customer's VPC pattern aligns with our edge connection drops — we think when the NAT gateway scales, ephemeral port mapping changes lead to RST on long-lived HTTP/2 streams. We'll validate with packet captures (if customer can do) or full VPC flow logs.

nate: Action items:
- eng-infra: correlate edge connections to NAT IPs and collect tcpdump if possible (nate)
- support: share mitigation and ask for VPC flow logs (julie)
- product/devex: consider SDK change to default to http1 for short-lived Lambda-style invocations (taylor)

julie: Shared mitigation note to customer and asked for VPC flow logs. Customer provided flow logs with time ranges. I uploaded to the incident.

support-bot: Incident INC-20260317-1376 updated: eng-infra investigating upstream connection churn. Next update ETA 20m.

taylor: Quick log sample from edge for context:
```
edge-conn: client_ip=10.0.5.12:56789 -> edge 54.182.x.x:443
upstream: host=gpu-serve-12 pool-3
event: reset upstream by peer after 12000ms
```

nate: Confirmed: matched flow logs show NAT IP reassign around same second as RST. Root cause hypothesis: NAT port reuse/eviction during scale leads to connection tear — affects HTTP/2 more due to multiplexed streams relying on single connection. Non-streaming sometimes pick up new connection but streaming breaks mid-stream.

samir: Proposed next steps for remediation:
- short-term: recommend SDK keepalive=false or prefer http1 for ephemeral workloads
- mid-term: edge should detect client IP churn and gracefully retry streams on compatible fallback connection (we can implement conservative reconnect logic)
- long-term: document best practices (lambda patterns, keepalive configs)

olivia: Customer asked for an official status note to share with their infra team. I posted the draft to them; they appreciated the root cause and are rolling the workaround.

julie: I'll update INC and notify account manager. Closing loop with customer once eng-infra posts final RCA.

nate: Eng-infra will follow up with a PR for a reconnect heuristic and coordinate with devex on SDK defaults. Marking monitoring to alert if similar NAT churn >2% in an AZ.

olivia: Thanks everyone. Will update when we have the RCA and timeline.
